cards_resequenced.change: authored by TRIAGE under R-099. Nothing we run noticed, because every check we have asks whether what is present is correct and none of them asks whether something that was there has gone. This card puts every piece back exactly as it was, in one change.

authored by TRIAGE under R-099, and it cannot be started until the restore above lands. the credential shutdown gains a second thing it must wait for, ruled under R-101 and landed by the restore card rather than here. Neither is true while a second, automatic path writes the live database and records nothing, so the shutdown would take away the controlled path and leave the uncontrolled one running.

escalations.title: The moment a database change is approved and merged, it goes straight into the live database on its own, with nobody running it and nothing checking it first. Every safety rule we wrote assumes a person or a script does that step. This was proved twice on 2026-09-03, then the card carrying the question was deleted by a merge the same night, so it has never actually reached you.
escalations.recommendation: KEEP the automatic path, and rewrite the rules to describe what actually happens, but only after we add a check that refuses any database change containing a row-deleting instruction before it can be merged. That check is small, it is the same parse we already do elsewhere, and it restores the one protection the automatic path removes. Why keep it rather than switch it off: it has already applied at least six changes correctly and the friction it saves is real, while the whole danger sits in the row-deleting class, which the check covers completely. IF UNANSWERED: every database change merged from now on reaches the live database with no pre-check, no assertion, no after-check and no record, and the rule saying row-deleting changes are never applied automatically protects nothing. Nothing else is blocked by this.

escalations.title: The extraction supplier has been told in writing that four database changes are still waiting to be switched on. They were switched on days ago. That paragraph is in the handover file we send him and it is false today.
escalations.recommendation: Correct the paragraph before the next message to him: the nineteenth paint category and the tonne and litre units are live now, not pending. Nothing is asked of him and nothing he has already built changes, so this is a factual correction rather than a request. WHILE YOU ARE THERE, ONE TIME-BOXED FACT: the sample document link he is using expires 2026-09-04 at 19:58 UTC, and regenerating it is one command on our side. IF UNANSWERED: he keeps planning around a switch-on date that has already passed, and the next thing he asks us about will be built on it. Low cost, but it is the second time our own stale record has reached someone outside the company.

escalations.title: Two settings for the low-stock warning email in the live hosting environment were put in front of you on 2026-08-31 and never answered. They are still the first two of three things standing between us and a warning email that actually arrives.
escalations.recommendation: Set RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM in the PRODUCTION environment and reply that they are set. Both are already required items on the credential shutdown list, so doing them now removes two items from that day rather than adding any. THE SAME HONEST CAVEAT AS LAST TIME: this does not make the readiness condition pass on its own. A third thing is needed, a recipient address on a domain that exists, and that one lands with the real staff accounts. IF UNANSWERED: nothing breaks. The warning email keeps recording its reason on screen and not sending, which is the designed behaviour, and both settings simply wait to be done on shutdown day.
